description:
Two substances, each filed as two rows, for the two ways a ceiling COMPARISON can go wrong that drug-reference-substance-dosing-ceilings.json cannot reach. Neither pair carries an ATC code, so no relevance gate can inject the second row for a reason other than the question naming the substance, and every band spans 0-120 so a patient's age never silences one.

Tinidazole 2000 / 500 is the ORDER pair: its ceilings disagree under numeric and lexicographic comparison, where every multi-row pair in that other file (3000/2000, 300/150, 4000/300, 4000/2000, 50/25, 60/30, 100/200) sorts identically either way, so a sort of the ceiling SPELLINGS passes every case built on it while a sort of the NUMBERS is what production has to do. Here "2000" sorts before "500" as text and 500 before 2000 as a number. It matters because DosingCeilingFidelityCheck reads position 0 as the strictest and returns as soon as the answer states it: with the list reversed, an answer quoting the LAXER ceiling finds it at position 0, the walk goes silent, and the check stops seeing exactly the defect issue #276 reports — with nothing else in the suite going red. The two rows publish the same mg/kg band, so their dosing NUMBERS differ only in the ceiling; their names differ too, as any two rows of a substance must.

Levothyroxine 5 / 0.5 is the DECIMAL pair, and it exists because the ceilings are the first NUMERIC needles this module scans an answer for. DrugReference.formatNumber emits Double.toString for a non-integral value, so this substance publishes "5 mg/day" and "0.5 mg/day" — and the laxer one's spelling is a SUFFIX of a decimal a clinical answer can easily contain. ChartSearchAiUtils.statesWord bounds a needle on letters and digits alone, so it reads "2.5 mg/day" as stating "5 mg/day": a decimal point is neither. That is a false POSITIVE on a published key, the one direction this check must never fail in, which is why the ceilings are scanned with statesMeasurement instead. A pair whose ceilings are both integral cannot show it, and no other fixture here has a non-integral ceiling at all. Its two rows also differ in mg/kg, where the order pair's agree — so the two pairs are not two copies of one arrangement, and a change that collapsed the other-rows item to its ceiling alone would still leave this pair saying something the other does not.
